notes: Run-created patterns (new_patterns.json): validates, predicts. Edges using run-created patterns: 2 (i=52 predicts PASS, i=53 predicts PASS) -> new-pattern edge pass rate 2/2. validates created but unused. Missed opportunities for earlier-run new patterns: edge 10 (avalanche model = finite-difference approximation of continuous model) should be equivalent_formulation, extracted as compares (FAIL). Also noteworthy: edges 13/14 ('We neglect the dependence of bulk density/repose angle on material composition') judged PASS on the grounds that 'neglect' acknowledges the physical dependence while excluding it from the model - but the KB edge loses the neglected status (design flag). Edge 51 is the opposite and worse: 'does not depend on external conditions' extracted WITH external conditions as input.

failures.nodes: output=operator of segregation; input=granular material composition in surface flow; parameter=composition of the layer generated at the surface
failures.evidence: The operator of segregation relates the granular material composition in surface flow to the composition of the layer generated at the surface of a growing pile or filling.
failures.reason: law-as-output category confusion: the operator IS the law; the layer composition is the law's OUTPUT but is bound to the parameter slot

failures.nodes: from=model @11# of avalanche mixing; to=simple continuous flow mixing model
failures.evidence: Mathematically, the model @11# of avalanche mixing in a rotating drum is a finite difference approximation of a simple continuous flow mixing model.
failures.reason: derivation/approximation identity ('X is a finite-difference approximation of Y') extracted as a side-by-side comparison; equivalent_formulation (in meta, created run 2) is the right pattern and was not used

failures.nodes: from=complicated model of transverse flow; to=simulation of mixing of equal but differently colored granules
failures.evidence: A much more complicated model of transverse flow has been recently proposed and used in simulation of mixing of equal but differently colored granules @13#.
failures.reason: uses-relation inverted into background: the model was USED IN the simulation; neither is background for the other

failures.nodes: source=percolation of small particles; target=bulk of material
failures.evidence: the percolation of small particles through the bulk of material is also neglected
failures.reason: a neglected phenomenon ('percolation through the bulk') is not an influence of percolation ON the bulk; no dependence between the two nodes is stated

failures.nodes: source=free surface of a filling; target=angle of repose
failures.evidence: the free surface of a filling is initially flat and, as the rotation starts, becomes inclined approximately at the angle of repose
failures.reason: geometric evolution (surface inclines TO the repose angle) contains no influence of the surface on the angle; the angle characterizes the surface's final slope

failures.evidence: all mixing and segregation occur in a thin surface layer
failures.reason: spatial confinement of processes to a layer is not an influence of the layer on the concentration kappa

failures.evidence: V is the velocity in the rotating bulk and V_n is the value at the free surface of the component of V normal to this surface
failures.reason: subject 'speed' does not occur in the sentence at all (concept conflation with rotation speed); the sentence defines V_n as the normal component of V

failures.evidence: kappa_- is the composition of a bulk layer that has just arrived at this surface
failures.reason: definitional statement about kappa_-; no influence between the surface coordinate s and the bulk layer is stated; source=s is spurious

failures.evidence: it is necessary to know the operator of segregation which ... determines the local composition of a generated surface layer: kappa_-(s,t) = S(kappa_+(s,t))
failures.reason: object slot binds the surface coordinate s; the operator's defining formula kappa_- = S(kappa_+) is what should be bound

failures.nodes: source=midpoint flux concentration; target=ordinary differential equation
failures.evidence: The midpoint flux concentration kappa_0^1 serves as the initial condition for ordinary differential equation ~3!
failures.reason: serving as an initial condition for an ODE is not an influence relation, and an equation is not a dependent quantity

failures.evidence: Each step of the numerical simulation should consist of ~1! determining the midpoint flux concentration kappa_0^1 from Eq. ~5!; ~2! ...
failures.reason: a quantity computed within a simulation step is not a structural component of the simulation

failures.nodes: source=mean tracer position; target=type of material
failures.evidence: the mean tracer position is not affected by the type of material
failures.reason: NEGATED influence extracted as positive: 'not affected by' states independence

failures.evidence: A smooth monotone interpolation ... is given, e.g., by the parametric representation where tau in [0,1] is a parameter
failures.reason: tau is a PARAMETER of the representation, not its definition; 'X is parameterized by Y' is not 'X is defined-as Y'

failures.nodes: from=this relation; to=operator of surface segregation
failures.evidence: In this work we employed this relation, which is supposedly independent of geometrical configuration, to simulate the size segregation of binary mixture in a rotating drum.
failures.reason: the two nodes are two guises of the SAME entity (the relation IS the operator, employed unchanged); the real content - porting it to the new drum configuration (adapts) - is not captured

failures.nodes: output=segregation properties of polydisperse granular material; parameter=operator of surface segregation; input=external conditions
failures.evidence: The segregation properties ... are characterized by a constitutive relation (the operator of segregation), which does not depend on these external conditions and can be identified experimentally.
failures.reason: POLARITY INVERSION: the sentence says the relation does NOT depend on external conditions; the edge binds external conditions as an input, asserting the opposite
